html:
German poet, playwright, novelist and scientist, born in Frankfurt in 1749. He is the central figure of German literature.

He became famous at twenty five with The Sorrows of Young Werther (1774), the letters of a young man who kills himself over an impossible love. It swept Europe and made him the voice of the Sturm und Drang movement.

In 1775 he moved to the small duchy of Weimar, where he served as a minister and stayed for the rest of his life. A long trip to Italy in the 1780s turned him toward classical calm. With his friend Friedrich Schiller he made Weimar the centre of German letters.

His life's work was Faust, the scholar who makes a pact with the devil, written over some sixty years; the second part came out only after his death in 1832. He also wrote poems, novels and works on plant forms and on colour. He met Napoleon, who had read Werther several times.
